claims.text: The local catalog models Toyota Auto Campaign with an October-December 1997 source-month range.
The local source slice models two source-pinned card identities for this campaign lane: Arcanine and Pikachu.
The campaign is represented as a Toyota Auto dealership pamphlet / campaign route, not as a booster set, deck, or ordinary expansion release.

The local snapshot says the Toyota Pikachu is an alternate-art reprint related to the November 1996 CoroCoro Comic Pikachu lane, while Arcanine was later printed with the Pokemon Song Best Collection CD and is described there as identical to the Toyota pamphlet version.
The current local card rows carry provider metadata crediting Ken Sugimori on both modeled Toyota Auto Campaign rows.
The Toyota Auto Campaign matters because it shows Pokemon cards leaving hobby/magazine channels and entering ordinary family errands: a car dealership pamphlet could become a card-memory route.

Because this is a source-pinned two-card campaign slice with reuse paths on both cards, an agent must identify the Toyota route separately from the Pokemon Song Best Arcanine route, the CoroCoro Pikachu lane, and ordinary Base-style Arcanine/Pikachu rows.

narrative.human_title: Toyota Auto Campaign — the dealership pamphlet becomes a card route
narrative.why_it_matters: Toyota Auto is one of those tiny distribution stories that makes early Pokemon feel alive. The cards were not only in packs, magazines, decks, and tournament envelopes; they could appear in a car dealership pamphlet, carried home by a family doing something completely outside the hobby. Arcanine and Pikachu make the route easy to love, but the deeper charm is the route itself: Pokemon learning to travel through ordinary Japanese retail life.

narrative.human_title: Toyota Arcanine — the same beast, two routes
narrative.why_it_matters: Arcanine is the card that makes this little campaign feel bigger than a checklist. It is not only a Toyota pamphlet promo; the same presentation echoes into Song Best, where Pokemon music carried cards as physical souvenirs. For a collector, that means the card has two kinds of beauty: the monster on the cardboard, and the route by which that cardboard entered someone's life.

narrative.human_title: Toyota Pikachu — the mascot takes the family car route
narrative.why_it_matters: Toyota Pikachu is charming because it makes perfect franchise sense. Pikachu was already becoming the friendly face that could cross from manga to rules sheets to errands with your parents. Here the mascot is not only collectible; it is a little ambassador, carrying Pokemon out of the hobby shop and into the showroom.
